material_definitions: NASICON-type Li1+xAlxTi2-x(PO4)3 (LATP) is a promising solid electrolyte for lithium-ion batteries.
The sample studied is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) ceramic pellet.
The LATP ceramic pellet shows a total ionic conductivity of 1.12 x 10^-3 S/cm.
The study investigates LISICON-structured solid solutions including Li3P1-xVxO4, Li3+xV1-xGexO4, and Li3+xP1-xGexO4 with x ranging from 0 to 1.
X-ray powder diffraction revealed that the samples were phase pure, with reflections indexed to previously reported crystal structures and space groups.
The unit cell volumes of Li3P1-xVxO4 and Li3+xP1-xGexO4 were found to increase with increasing Ge4+ and V5+ content, while Li3+xV1-xGexO4 showed little variation.
Aliovalent substitution creating partial lithium occupancy in these LISICONs led to a 4-5 order of magnitude increase in ionic conductivity compared to parent Li3PO4 and Li3VO4 phases.
The pre-exponential factor of lithium-ion conductivity was found to scale with the activation energy for all samples, following the Meyer-Neldel rule.
